title: Output planes for a 4224 x 2816 picture: seven 4K-layout planes of 14,942,208 bytes, the eighth out of the pool, and the HD layout's plane enlarged
status: built from the firmware's file and run in the FX3's own allocator; NEVER RUN ON A CAMERA. The same ten words with 14,745,600 ran on an FX6 (dmm7slot_fx6_v1)
credit: the memory model, the seven-plane idea and the ten words: github.com/ArcaneLantern/fx6-open-gate-test issue 2 (Mininoob)
table: unit records 0x1f7f90c .. 0x1f85730 (parse_dmmcfg.RAM fx3_702): record = base + seq x 0x14, {0, type, key, size, attributes}
why: the FX3 fills an output plane at 1.25 bytes per pixel: 13,271,040 bytes hold 3840 x 2560 (12,288,000); 4224 x 2816 needs 14,868,480

sites.note: HD layout 0x28, its one 4K plane: size 13,271,040 -> 14,942,208 (the layout is then over its parent, as on the FX6)
